## Series Overview

Most agentic AI tutorials jump straight to "build a LangGraph agent" without ever showing why
each piece exists, or what a plain (non-agentic) baseline even looks like. This series starts
there instead: one running use case, X-ray void detection on a synthetic dataset with exact ground truth, carried all the
way from a bare CV model with zero agentic anything, through tool calling and structured output,
into a real multi-node LangGraph pipeline, then multi-agent orchestration, RAG, fine-tuning,
VLM-first architectures, and finally the production concerns (evaluation, cost, deployment,
monitoring) that tutorials usually skip.

A companion series, [Agentic Architecture: Supply Chain](../agentic-supply-chain/index.qmd),
takes the same architecture built here and re-applies it to a completely different domain --
proof that the pattern, not the domain data, is the reusable part.

Two more series are planned to follow this one (both coming soon): an
[agentic AI software factory for the inspection system](../agentic-factory-inspection/index.qmd), where agents
take tickets and change the pipeline built here behind a gate they cannot edit, and an
[agentic AI software factory for robust segmentation models](../agentic-factory-segmentation/index.qmd), where agents
run the experiments that build a better detector for it.

This is a roadmap post: links go live as each part is written, in order.

:::{.callout-note}
**Rewritten on 2026-10-18.** Parts 1 to 8 first ran on the public GDXray casting radiographs. GDXray
is free for research and education only and does not allow redistribution, so I rebuilt the whole
series on a [synthetic void dataset](../agentic-factory-segmentation/01-synthetic-void-dataset.qmd)
that I generate myself, with fresh runs, new numbers and new animations. Several conclusions
changed, and each post says where.
:::

### Arc 1 -- Foundations

1. [Introduction -- why agentic AI, why X-ray defect detection as the teaching example](01-introduction.qmd)
2. [The dataset and the baseline model](02-dataset-baseline.qmd) -- the synthetic void dataset,
   a plain classical CV detector, no agent yet, scored honestly against exact ground truth
3. [Your first tool-calling LLM](03-first-tool-call.qmd) -- wrapping the detector as a "tool",
   one LLM call that reads structured output and writes a plain-English explanation
4. [Prompting and structured output -- getting reliable JSON/structured responses from the LLM](04-prompting-structured-output.qmd)
   about defect type, severity, confidence

### Arc 2 -- The Agent Loop

5. [What makes it an "agent"](05-what-makes-an-agent.qmd) -- planning, tool use, memory, control flow;
   a hand-written agent loop, scored against real ground truth
6. [Building the graph](06-building-the-graph.qmd) -- LangGraph basics: state, nodes, edges;
   the Part 5 loop redrawn as a graph, with a pause-and-resume demo and tests for every edge
7. [The inspection pipeline](07-the-inspection-pipeline.qmd) -- classify defect, check business
   rules, decide, report, as a real LangGraph graph where the code owns the order and the model
   owns two judgments; scored on held-out frames, with the model's guidance taken away as a control
8. [Tool design](08-tool-design.qmd) -- plain code vs. a small typed model vs. a language model,
   measured head to head on two real calls from the Part 7 pipeline (is this box a real defect? what does
   this note say?): a rule, the open-source [Laya](https://huggingface.co/convaiinnovations/laya)
   (Apache-2.0, runs locally) and the local Qwen3-Coder, compared on accuracy, calibration, latency and
   tokens. [TypeSafe's Jev](https://typesafe.ai) (hosted) was meant to be the other typed model, but I had no
   API access: its adapter is written and not run, and the post says so. The typed models' probabilities are
   what the review-vs-escalate threshold in post 9 would be set on
9. Human-in-the-loop -- flagging uncertain cases for review, approval workflows

### Arc 3 -- Scaling Up: Multi-Agent and Deep Agents

10. When one agent isn't enough -- sub-agents per defect category or per inspection stage
11. Deep Agents harness -- planning, virtual filesystem, context management for long-running
    investigations
12. Orchestration patterns -- supervisor agents, delegation, aggregating sub-agent results
13. Wayfinder-style planning -- handling investigations that span multiple sessions, ticket-based
    maps for open-ended defect investigations

### Arc 4 -- Knowledge and Precision

14. [Context engineering starts with retrieval](14-context-engineering-retrieval.qmd) -- grep, paged reads,
    offloading, paths instead of payloads and sub-agents that see one file, measured on this series' own archive
    (a 4,000-row CSV, 200 pipeline reports, DINOv3 + LanceDB visual search). Stuffing the prompt wins when the
    archive fits; the harness wins when it does not. Replaces the earlier "RAG over your defect catalog" plan; what to
    embed is in [Retrieval and RAG](../agentic-development/09-retrieval-rag.qmd)
15. Building the retrieval pipeline -- chunking, embeddings, vector store, evaluation of
    retrieval quality
16. Fine-tuning -- when RAG isn't enough, fine-tuning a model on your labeled defect explanations
    and decisions for domain precision
17. Vision-language models -- letting the model reason directly over the X-ray image instead of
    only structured detector output; comparing VLM-first vs. CV-model-first architectures

### Arc 5 -- Production and Evaluation

18. Evaluation -- building an eval set, using LangSmith (or similar) to trace and score agent
    decisions
19. Cost and latency tuning -- model selection per step, caching, batching
20. Failure handling -- retries, fallbacks, graceful degradation
21. Deployment -- turning the pipeline into a real triggered service
22. Monitoring in production -- drift detection, feedback loops, continuous improvement

### Arc 6 -- Expert-Level Topics

23. Security and safety for agents -- prompt injection risks when reading external documents or
    web content, guardrails around autonomous actions vs. actions requiring human approval
24. Multi-agent communication protocols and standards -- how agents talk to each other, emerging
    standards in the field
25. Agent memory design -- long-term vs. short-term memory, deciding what an agent should remember
    across sessions vs. what it should forget
26. Cost and business ROI framing -- justifying an agent project to management, measuring time
    saved and errors caught, not just technical cost/latency tuning
27. Testing and simulation -- testing an agent before production using simulated and adversarial
    scenarios, not just live evaluation
28. Choosing an agent framework -- the broader landscape beyond LangGraph and Deep Agents, how to
    evaluate and pick a framework for a given use case
29. Versioning and change management for agents -- prompts, tools, and models drift over time; how
    to version agent behavior and roll back safely when a change breaks production

### Capstone

30. Putting it all together -- the finished inspection pipeline, lessons learned, and the bridge into the two
    factory series: what the pipeline needs before agents are allowed to change it, and the gates and
    controls that make that safe
